title: Portrait of a Needle Galaxy
caption: The needle-thin galaxy IC 2233, imaged by the Mayall 4-meter Telescope at Kitt Peak
credit: KPNO/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA. · Acknowledgments: · PI: M T. Patterson (New Mexico State University). Image processing: Travis Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage), Mahdi Zamani & Davide de Martin

recognition.text: NOIRLab Image of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: IC 2233 is an unusually thin galaxy, its profile as slender as a needle. That shape comes from its structure together with the way it is oriented toward Earth.

Astronomers call a galaxy's tilt its inclination, and IC 2233 is seen almost exactly edge-on, which makes it one of the flattest galaxies known. It also lacks the prominent central bulge that thickens the profile of spirals such as Andromeda and the Milky Way. The exposure is deep, and the whole field is scattered with other galaxies tilted at all sorts of angles.

The galaxy's wafer-thin shape has intrigued observers for nearly 150 years. It was discovered in 1874 by Isaac Roberts, a Welsh amateur astronomer who was one of the pioneers of photographing the sky.

understand.summary: The Mosaic I camera on the Mayall 4-meter Telescope observed IC 2233 through U, B and R filters plus a hydrogen-alpha filter, spanning near-ultraviolet and visible light. The colors assigned to each filter are not published.
